title: Refresh an expiring token during a VCF Networks vCenter batch
prompt: Complete the PowerShell module in `src/Vcf.OperationsNetworks/Vcf.OperationsNetworks.psm1` by implementing `Add-VcfOperationsNetworksVCenterBatch`. The function must use the installed `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops` PowerCLI prerequisite version 13.4.0.24798382 (including its username/password model initializer) and the VCF Operations for Networks 9.0 REST contract in `docs/contract.json`; do not vendor VMware modules. Authenticate with the contract's `create` operation, then submit every input vCenter with `addVcenterDatasource` and return the created objects in input order. During the batch the current NetworkInsight token can expire: on a 401, obtain a fresh token and retry the current vCenter without replaying any vCenter that already succeeded. Construct contract-shaped JSON rather than serializing SDK/input objects wholesale, so optional properties that are unset, null, or empty are omitted while explicitly supplied boolean `false` values are preserved. Only `src/Vcf.OperationsNetworks/Vcf.OperationsNetworks.psm1` is editable; keep the module manifest, contract, provenance, and tests unchanged. The included loopback service is the test endpoint and no live VMware endpoint is needed. Run `python3 tests/verify.py` to verify the integration.
reference_setup: pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command "if (-not (Get-Module -ListAvailable -Name VMware.OpenAPI | Where-Object Version -eq '13.4.0.24798382')) { Install-Module VMware.OpenAPI -RequiredVersion 13.4.0.24798382 -Scope CurrentUser -Force -AllowClobber -Repository PSGallery }; if (-not (Get-Module -ListAvailable -Name VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops | Where-Object Version -eq '13.4.0.24798382')) { Install-Module VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops -RequiredVersion 13.4.0.24798382 -Scope CurrentUser -Force -AllowClobber -Repository PSGallery }"
